title: Fixing before replacing
description: A repair is often cheaper, faster, and greener than a replacement — here is how to judge.

body.heading: The repair question
paragraphs: When something breaks, pause before replacing. Ask: What exactly is broken? Is it a part that can be replaced, a skill I can learn, or a job for a local repairer? Many failures are small parts wearing out, not whole products dying.
Online repair guides and videos cover an enormous range of common fixes, and community repair cafés in many towns will help you fix items free or cheaply.

body.heading: Do the honest maths
paragraphs: Compare the repair cost with replacement, but include the hidden costs of new: delivery, setup, disposing of the old item, and learning a new device. Repair often wins by more than the sticker comparison suggests.
Safety first, though: electrical, gas, and structural repairs belong to qualified professionals. A wise fix knows its limits.

body.heading: Care prevents repairs
paragraphs: Cleaning filters, descaling, updating software, and storing things dry prevent many breakdowns entirely. Ten minutes of care beats a weekend of repair.

takeaway: When something breaks, diagnose first — many fixes are small, cheap, and satisfying.
